relays.notes: Serves kind-4 and kind-1059 back on demand, unauthenticated. Measured 2026-09-01: accepted writes and returned stored DMs on every attempt. Promoted to primary because the courier's rendezvous must be READABLE, not merely writable.

0xchat's own relay. Measured 2026-09-01: accepts and serves back both kind-4 and kind-1059. Added after it was the only relay that reliably round-tripped a test DM during the 2026-09-01 courier investigation.

Intermittent. Measured 2026-09-01: served DM reads on 1 of 3 attempts, connection timeouts on the other 2; earlier the same day it refused one publish and accepted an identical event seconds later. Usable but never to be relied on alone.

DEMOTED 2026-09-01, was primary. Accepts writes and CANNOT serve DMs back to anyone: it demands NIP-42 AUTH for kind-4 and kind-1059 filters, then rejects every AUTH with 'relay needs serviceUrl to be configured before AUTH can work'. Neither the Secure Courier's drain nor the recipient's own client can read a DM out of it. As primary it silently broke operator credential delivery — see tollbooth-dpyc#249. Kept for non-DM traffic; must not be first. Also returned HTTP 502 for hours on 2026-09-02 while an operator was trying to bootstrap. Kept last so the list never shrinks to nothing, never relied upon.

caveat: Reachability is measured FROM SOMEWHERE. Cloudflare-fronted relays serve residential IPs and refuse datacenter ones: on 2026-09-02 relay.0xchat.com returned 403 and relay.damus.io 503 to an operator on Horizon while both answered a laptop normally. A relay that measures well here may still be unreachable from where the operators actually run, so this list is ranked on evidence and sized for redundancy — never trimmed to the winners.
